title: Why the Whole Can Still Destabilize When Everyone Correctly Protects Their Own Position
summary: Maintenance protects the continuity of one runtime; when several runtimes share resources and consequences, locally correct choices can still combine into system-level instability.
shortAnswer: Maintenance protects the continuity of one runtime; when several runtimes share resources and consequences, locally correct choices can still combine into system-level instability.
displayQuestion: Why the Whole Can Still Destabilize When Everyone Correctly Protects Their Own Position

blocks.text: At the end of Part Eight, maintenance reaches a problem it cannot solve alone: several runtimes can each be doing something locally correct while jointly creating a new instability. One person can accurately reduce load, yet the responsibility they leave still has to go somewhere; one department can reasonably protect scarce resources, while doing so reduces the operating space of another department.

This is the coordination threshold. Maintenance first asks “how can I continue?” Coordination begins asking “how can we continue at the same time?” Once time, resources, responsibility, risk, and consequences are shared, optimizing every local position separately does not guarantee a sustainable whole.

Coordination is not another word for maintenance. Maintenance can restore capacity, release residue, and repair a local structure. Coordination must additionally decide how multiple continuities relate: who uses scarce resources first, who yields temporarily, which boundaries remain protected, and where costs ultimately land.

At this layer, value, power, fairness, and exit capacity enter the runtime. Different participants do not have equal negotiating power. If “shared responsibility” depends on one position lacking a real ability to refuse, visible stability may simply be hiding transferred cost.

Mature maintenance therefore needs to know where it ends. It can stabilize one runtime, but it cannot by itself decide the most legitimate distribution among several runtimes. After the coordination threshold is crossed, reality needs a higher-level structure capable of seeing shared costs and shared constraints.

blocks.heading: Key judgment
blocks.statement: Local correctness does not automatically produce global sustainability.

blocks.question: When one position successfully reduces its cost, where does that cost go?
